docs.title: Analytics Tagging Playbook
docs.text:
Our standard way of tagging websites and apps with Adobe Analytics and Google Analytics 4. Use it before you build a new implementation, when you review someone else's, and when a client asks "how should we track this?".

Every tag has two parts:

  • A developer specification: the data layer push, when to fire it, and what each key holds. Give this to the client's developers.
  • A tagging setup for our team: the data elements, rules and variable mappings for each implementation type. Custom code only where needed.
Implementation Developers push to Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement) adobeDataLayer Adobe Web SDK (XDM) adobeDataLayer Adobe Mobile SDK Mobile SDK calls, same keys Google Analytics 4 (GTM) dataLayer

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
I need to track... Read eVars Events GA4 dimensions Installing the tag manager Library Installation Where visitors came from Marketing Channels 0 0 0 What page they are on Page Naming 1 0 1 Which part of the site Site Sections 1 0 3 What they searched for Site Search 3 2 2 Forms started and completed Form Tracking 4 4 4 Any link, button or banner click Universal Clickthrough 3 1 3 Downloads File Downloads 3 1 3 Errors Error Tracking 2 1 2 Video plays and how much was watched Video Tracking 2 5 2 Article and content metadata Content Page Tracking up to 9 1 up to 9

These pages are drafts

Every page is marked Draft until a team lead reviews it. The counts are our recommended starting point, not Adobe or Google rules. Check them against each client's available variables.

docs.title: Rules of the playbook
docs.text:
1. Tags never use real eVar or event numbers. They use placeholders like EVAR_FORM_NAME, so they work for any client.
  2. Never send personal data (names, ID numbers, account numbers, email addresses) in any variable.
  3. Keys and event names are the same on every platform. Only the data layer array changes.
  4. If a page is wrong or missing something, fix it. See How to contribute.

docs.title: How to contribute
docs.text: Anyone on the team can add or change a page. You do not need to install anything.

docs.title: Fix or improve an existing page (2 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Open the page on the site.
  2. Click the pencil icon at the top right of the page.
  3. Change the text, then click Commit changes and choose Create a new branch and start a pull request.
  4. Write one line saying what you changed. Submit.

docs.title: Add a new topic (for example, e-commerce)
docs.text:
1. Open docs/tags/ on GitHub.
  2. Click Add file > Create new file. Name it in lower case with hyphens, for example ecommerce.md.
  3. Open templates/tag.md, copy everything, and paste it into your new file.
  4. In the line under the title, keep the status as Draft and fill in your name and today's date, for example 29-Oct-2026.
  5. Fill in what you know. Delete any section you cannot fill, but keep "Variables required" and "Developer specification". Rough is fine; reviewers will help.
  6. Add one line to the menu in mkdocs.yml, under the section that fits (see the table below).
  7. Add a row for it to the "where to start" table on the home page, with the same counts as its "Variables required" section.
  8. Submit as a pull request.

docs.title: Which menu section?
docs.text: Section For Setup Things developers install or build once: the tag manager, the data layer Analytics Config Settings made in the analytics tool itself, with little or no developer work Core tags Tracking for something visitors do or see: pages, search, forms, clicks, downloads, errors, video Supporting config Techniques that support other tags, such as event serialization Testing QA and debugging

docs.title: What a good page contains
docs.text:
• A developer specification: the data layer push (JSON), when it fires, what each key holds with example values. A developer should be able to build it from this alone.
  • Tagging setup for each implementation type: the data elements, rules and variable mappings. Write custom code only if a rule cannot do it.
  • The number of eVars, props and events (and Google Analytics custom dimensions and events).
  • A QA checklist.

docs.title: What a reviewer checks
docs.text:
• It says how many variables and events are needed, and the home page shows the same counts.
  • It uses placeholders, not real eVar or event numbers.
  • Keys and event names are the same across platforms.
  • It was tested once, and the QA section says how.
  • No client names or personal data. Use made-up example values.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
• A lead reviews the pull request and may ask for changes.
  • Once merged, the page publishes to the site automatically, marked Draft.
  • When it has been tested on a real project, a lead changes its status from Draft to Approved.

docs.title: Page statuses
docs.text: Status Meaning Draft Someone wrote it; nobody senior has reviewed and tested it yet Approved Reviewed and tested; use it on projects Deprecated Don't use for new work; the page says what replaced it

docs.title: Writing tips
docs.text:
• Write for a new colleague who has never seen the client's setup.
  • Show a good and a bad example of every value.
  • Keep custom code short and say what each part does.
  • Link to other pages instead of repeating them.
  • When a spec changes, say so in the page's Notes, as a changelog line with date and name.

docs.title: How the playbook is organised
docs.text:
Our usual way of working is: we write a specification, developers push a small JSON object to the data layer, and we build the tags. So each tag has two parts:

  1. Developer specification. The exact data layer push, when it fires, and what each key holds. Give this section to the website or app developers.
  2. Tagging setup. The data elements, rules and variable mappings we create in Adobe Launch or Google Tag Manager. We only write custom code when a rule cannot do the job without it, and those snippets are labelled Custom code (only if needed).

docs.title: Data layer names
docs.text:
Platform Array developers push to Adobe Analytics and Adobe Web SDK (via Launch) window.adobeDataLayer Google Analytics 4 (via Google Tag Manager) window.dataLayer Mobile apps No data layer. Developers call the Mobile SDK with the same keys

The keys and event names are identical on every platform, so one spec serves all of them. Only the array name changes.

Always start a push with the line that creates the array, in case the library has not loaded yet:

window.adobeDataLayer = window.adobeDataLayer || [];

docs.title: Data layer key rules
docs.text:
• Event name in event, lower case with underscores: form_start.
  • Keys in camelCase: formName, universalClickthroughURL.
  • Keys are flat (no nested objects). The data layer remembers the last value of each key, so every push must send all the keys for its event. Otherwise a value from an earlier event can leak into the next one.
  • Values are readable text, exactly as listed in the spec (Contact us, not contact_us). We lower-case and trim them in Launch (data element options Force lowercase value and Remove extra whitespace).
  • Several values in one key: separate with a comma and a space (Supply Chain, Advanced Manufacturing).
  • No personal data. Ever.

docs.title: Placeholders instead of numbers
docs.text:
Clients have different variable layouts, so the playbook never says "use eVar11". It uses names in capitals:

Placeholder Means EVAR_FORM_NAME The eVar the client has chosen for the form name PROP_SEARCH_TERM The prop for the search term EVENT_FORM_START The success event for a form start

When you implement for a client, fill in their real numbers in a variable map kept with the project:

EVAR_FORM_NAME      -> eVar11
EVENT_FORM_START    -> event13

docs.title: The four implementation types
docs.text:
Every tag's tagging setup has these tabs, in this order. The tab you pick stays selected as you move between pages.

Tab Used when Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement) Websites with the Adobe Analytics extension in Launch Adobe Web SDK (XDM) Websites or apps sending data to Adobe Experience Platform Edge Adobe Mobile SDK Native iOS and Android apps Google Analytics 4 (GTM) Websites using Google Analytics 4 through Google Tag Manager

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• Launch rules: start with how it is triggered. PLR page load, EBR element-based (click, viewport, key press), DCR direct call, ACDL data layer event. Example: ACDL - Form: Start by "form_start".
  • Launch data elements: DL - keyName for data layer values (DL - formName), Query - name for URL parameters, Code - name for custom code.
  • GTM variables, triggers and tags: DLV - keyName (data layer variable), CE - event_name (custom event trigger), GA4 - Event Name (tag).
  • Variable names in the analytics tool: plain words for what the variable holds. Example: Form Name, not form_nm_v2.

docs.title: Respect privacy
docs.text:
Never send names, ID numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, account numbers or text typed by the visitor. If you are not sure, leave it out and ask a lead.

Check names against your own setup

Menu and field names in Launch, Adobe Experience Platform, Google Tag Manager and the Mobile SDK change between versions, and XDM schemas are often customised. Treat the setup steps as a guide and confirm them in your own property before shipping.

docs.title: Universal Clickthrough
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: One consistent way to track clicks on links, buttons and banners that lead to a new page, without building a rule for every element. It answers "what do people click, and where does it take them?".

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars 3 EVAR_CLICK_COMPONENT, EVAR_CLICK_LABEL, EVAR_CLICK_URL Props 0 Events 1 EVENT_UNIVERSAL_CLICK Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 3 Click Component, Click Label, Click URL Events 1 universal_click

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: On the click of any link on the site that leads to a new page. Downloads use File Downloads instead.

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM) Data element (Data Layer Computed State) Path DL - universalClickthroughComponent universalClickthroughComponent DL - universalClickthroughLabel universalClickthroughLabel DL - universalClickthroughURL universalClickthroughURL Rule Trigger Actions ACDL - Link: Universal Click by "universal_click" Data layer event universal_click Set Variables: EVAR_CLICK_COMPONENT, EVAR_CLICK_LABEL, EVAR_CLICK_URL, event EVENT_UNIVERSAL_CLICK. Then Send Beacon, custom link, name Universal Click

Keep the labels lower case (data element option) so Get in touch and Get in Touch become one value.

Same trigger and data elements. In the XDM object use the link fields that already exist:

XDM field Source eventType web.webinteraction.linkClicks web.webInteraction.name DL - universalClickthroughLabel web.webInteraction.URL DL - universalClickthroughURL web.webInteraction.type other web.webInteraction.linkClicks.value 1 _tenant.click.component (custom) DL - universalClickthroughComponent

Map web.webInteraction.name and URL to EVAR_CLICK_LABEL and EVAR_CLICK_URL, and the custom field to EVAR_CLICK_COMPONENT, in your Analytics mapping.

Processing Rules:

Condition Set Action name equals universal_click EVENT_UNIVERSAL_CLICK Context data universalClickthroughComponent exists EVAR_CLICK_COMPONENT Context data universalClickthroughLabel exists EVAR_CLICK_LABEL Context data universalClickthroughURL exists EVAR_CLICK_URL Item Setup Variables DLV - universalClickthroughComponent, DLV - universalClickthroughLabel, DLV - universalClickthroughURL Trigger CE - universal_click, Custom Event, event name universal_click Tag GA4 - Universal Click, GA4 Event universal_click, parameters click_component, click_label, click_url GA4 Admin Register the three parameters as event-scoped custom dimensions

GA4 collects its own click event for outbound links when enhanced measurement is on. Keep it on only if you want both.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Click a link: one hit, with the right component, label and URL
  • [ ] Click an icon inside a link: still one hit
  • [ ] The URL is the full destination, not a relative path
  • [ ] Download links send file_download, not universal_click

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Clicks that open in a new tab must send the hit before the page changes. Test with the Network tab set to Preserve log.

docs.title: Content Page Tracking
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text:
Describes articles, guides, case studies and similar content so the client can see which topics, industries and formats perform. Only for content pages. Normal pages (home, forms, product pages) must not fire it.

This is an optional topic. Choose only the keys the client will report on.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text:
Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars Up to 9 One per key you keep: EVAR_CONTENT_NAME, EVAR_CONTENT_TYPE, EVAR_CONTENT_TOPIC, EVAR_CONTENT_SEC_TOPICS, EVAR_CONTENT_INDUSTRY, EVAR_CONTENT_SOURCE, EVAR_CONTENT_PUB_DATE, EVAR_CONTENT_LENGTH, EVAR_CONTENT_FILE_SIZE Props 0 Events 1 EVENT_CONTENT_VIEW Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions Up to 9 One per key kept Events 1 content_view

A typical set is 5 to 6 keys: name, type, topic, industry, source and publication date.

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: Once the content page has loaded. Fire it in addition to the normal page view.

docs.title: Developer specification
docs.text:
Adobe websites (adobeDataLayer)Google Analytics websites (dataLayer)Mobile apps 
window.adobeDataLayer = window.adobeDataLayer || [];
window.adobeDataLayer.push({
  'event': 'content_view',
  'contentName': '<content name>',
  'contentType': '<content type>',
  'contentTopic': '<content topic>',
  'contentSecTopics': '<content secondary topics>',
  'contentIndustry': '<content industry>',
  'contentSource': '<content source>',
  'contentPublicationDate': '<content publication date>',
  'contentLengthByTime': '<content length by time>',
  'contentFileSize': '<content file size>'
});

window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
window.dataLayer.push({
  'event': 'content_view',
  'contentName': '<content name>',
  'contentType': '<content type>',
  'contentTopic': '<content topic>',
  'contentSecTopics': '<content secondary topics>',
  'contentIndustry': '<content industry>',
  'contentSource': '<content source>',
  'contentPublicationDate': '<content publication date>',
  'contentLengthByTime': '<content length by time>',
  'contentFileSize': '<content file size>'
});

MobileCore.track(action: "content_view", data: [
    "contentName": "<content name>", "contentType": "<content type>", "contentTopic": "<content topic>"
])
Key What it holds Expected values and examples contentName Name of the content page The article title, or the topic or category name for listing pages contentType Type of content. Use the agreed list Insights article, Case study article, Business guide article contentTopic Primary topic. One value from the agreed list Sustainability contentSecTopics Secondary topics. Several values separated by a comma and a space Supply Chain, Technology contentIndustry Industry focus. One value from the agreed list Logistics & Supply Chain Management contentSource Where the content came from Original, Partnered, Syndicated, Sponsored contentPublicationDate Date in dd mmm yyyy 27 Apr 2026 contentLengthByTime Reading time 8 min contentFileSize Download size (for e-books). Empty text if none 197KB, 5MB

The lists for type, topic, industry and source belong to each client. Keep them in the client's own spec, and use the same values everywhere. Send every key, with empty text ('') when it does not apply.

Example

{
  "event": "content_view",
  "contentName": "Five ways to reinvent your business",
  "contentType": "Insights article",
  "contentTopic": "Innovation",
  "contentSecTopics": "Supply Chain, Technology",
  "contentIndustry": "General",
  "contentSource": "Original",
  "contentPublicationDate": "27 Apr 2026",
  "contentLengthByTime": "8 min",
  "contentFileSize": ""
}

docs.title: Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM) Data element (Data Layer Computed State) Path DL - contentName and so on, one per key contentName, contentType, contentTopic, contentSecTopics, ... Rule Trigger Actions ACDL - Content: View by "content_view" Data layer event content_view Set Variables: each EVAR_CONTENT_* = its data element, event EVENT_CONTENT_VIEW. Send Beacon, custom link, Content View

Multi-value keys stay as one text value. If the client wants to report each secondary topic separately, use a list eVar (delimiter ,) in Adobe Admin.

XDM object with a custom content field group, one field per key, and event type content.view. Map the fields to the eVars in the Analytics mapping.

Processing Rules: action content_view sets EVENT_CONTENT_VIEW; each content... context data key sets its eVar.

Item Setup Variables DLV - contentName and so on, one per key Trigger CE - content_view Tag GA4 - Content View, event content_view, parameters content_name, content_type, content_topic, ... GA4 Admin Register each parameter you want to report on as a custom dimension. Skip high-cardinality ones, such as content_name, if you do not need them as a dimension

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Fires on content pages only
  • [ ] Every key is present, with empty text where it does not apply
  • [ ] Values match the agreed lists exactly
  • [ ] Multi-value keys use a comma and a space

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Publication date and reading time are text, not numbers. Keep the format fixed so reports sort and group correctly.

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this is and why
docs.text:
A data layer is a JavaScript array that the website pushes small objects into. Tags listen to the pushes and read the values, instead of scraping the page. When the site's design changes, tracking keeps working.

We use adobeDataLayer for Adobe and dataLayer for Google Tag Manager.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: None. The data layer feeds the variables on the other pages.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
window.adobeDataLayer = window.adobeDataLayer || [];
window.adobeDataLayer.push({
  'event': 'form_start',
  'formName': 'General enquiry'
});
  1. The first line creates the array if it does not exist yet.
  2. Each push sends one object. The object with an event key tells the tag manager that something happened.
  3. A rule listens for that event name and reads the other keys.

docs.title: Rules for developers
docs.text:
• One push per moment. One push for a form start, one for a click. Do not combine them.
  • Flat keys. No nested objects.
  • Send every key every time. The data layer remembers the last value of each key. If a push leaves a key out, the old value stays and can leak into the next event.
  • Fire at the right time. Pushes for "success" events run after the server confirms.
  • Plain text values. Use the readable values from the spec. No personal data.
  • Names exactly as spec'd. Keys are camelCase (formName), events are lower case with underscores (form_start).

docs.title: Developer specification
docs.text:
See the individual tags. The standard events are:

Event Tag page_view (optional) Page Naming, Site Sections search_results (Adobe) / view_search_results (Google) Site Search form_start, form_step, form_complete, form_error Form Tracking universal_click Universal Clickthrough file_download File Downloads site_error Error Tracking video_milestone Video Tracking content_view (optional) Content Page Tracking

docs.title: Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM)

Add the Adobe Client Data Layer extension in Launch. Create data elements of type Data Layer Computed State with the key as the path. Create rules triggered by the extension's data layer event, set to the event name. Menu names can differ slightly by extension version.

Same as the AppMeasurement tab for triggers and data elements. The XDM object data element then gathers the values into the XDM structure.

There is no data layer in apps. Developers call MobileCore.track(action:data:) (iOS) or MobileCore.trackAction (Android) with the same keys.

Create Data Layer Variable variables (Data Layer Version 2) and Custom Event triggers named after the event.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] In the browser console, type adobeDataLayer (or dataLayer): the pushes are listed
  • [ ] In Adobe, adobeDataLayer.getState() returns the combined values
  • [ ] The data layer exists before the library loads
  • [ ] Values change correctly on virtual page views

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Adobe also offers an event-driven data layer standard (Adobe Client Data Layer). The pushes shown here are compatible with it.

docs.title: Library Installation
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this covers and why
docs.text: The first thing developers add to the site is the tag manager's script, on every page. This page is the instruction to give them. Use the staging code on test sites and the production code on the live site, and keep the codes in the client's own spec.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: None.

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: On every page, as high in <head> as possible. Create the data layer array before the script, so pushes made early are not lost.

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
docs.text: Create one Launch property (or GTM container) per site, with development, staging and production environments. Publish to staging first and test (see QA and Debugging).

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The script is on every page, including error pages and the thank-you pages of forms
  • [ ] It loads once only
  • [ ] Staging code is not on the live site, and production code is not on staging
  • [ ] The data layer array exists before the script

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep the real embed URLs and container IDs out of this playbook. Put them in the client's own spec document.

docs.title: Error Tracking
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: Errors the visitor sees: 404 pages, server errors, failed payments. Shows where the experience breaks.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text:
Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars 2 EVAR_ERROR_TYPE, EVAR_ERROR_CODE Props 0 Events 1 EVENT_ERROR Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 2 Error Type, Error Code Events 1 site_error

Form validation errors use form_error from Form Tracking. This page is for everything else.

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: When the error is shown to the visitor.

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM) Data element (Data Layer Computed State) Path DL - errorType, DL - errorCode errorType, errorCode Rule Trigger Actions ACDL - Error: Site Error by "site_error" Data layer event site_error Set Variables: EVAR_ERROR_TYPE, EVAR_ERROR_CODE, event EVENT_ERROR. Send Beacon, custom link, Site Error

XDM object with a custom error field group (type, code) and a custom event type such as error.shown. Map to EVAR_ERROR_TYPE, EVAR_ERROR_CODE and EVENT_ERROR in the Analytics mapping.

Processing Rules: action site_error sets EVENT_ERROR. Context data errorType and errorCode set the two eVars.

Item Setup Variables DLV - errorType, DLV - errorCode Trigger CE - site_error Tag GA4 - Site Error, event site_error, parameters error_type, error_code GA4 Admin Register both as custom dimensions

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] A real 404 sends the push once
  • [ ] The values are codes, not message text

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: A 404 page should also send a page view with a page name that makes it easy to find (for example ...:error:404), see Page Naming.

docs.title: Event Serialization
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: Stops the same conversion being counted twice, for example when a visitor refreshes a thank-you page. Each submission has a unique ID, and Adobe ignores a repeat of the same ID on the same event.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text:
None. It uses the events you already have.

Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many Notes eVars 0 Events 0 Turn on serialization for the event in Admin (Success Events, serialization: use event ID) Type How many Notes Custom dimensions 0 Events 0 GA4 has no event serialization. See the Google Analytics 4 tab under Tagging setup

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: On events that must count once per action: form complete, application complete, purchase.

docs.title: Developer specification
docs.text:
The developers send a unique ID in the same push as the event. For forms this is submissionId (see Form Tracking).

Key What it holds Example submissionId A unique reference for this action, ideally returned by the server. Same value if the thank-you page reloads. Short, no personal data SUB-20261029-0042

If the server cannot supply one, the developers can create it once and keep it for the visit:

var id = sessionStorage.getItem('submissionId') || Date.now().toString(36);
sessionStorage.setItem('submissionId', id);

They must clear it when a new submission starts.

docs.title: Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM)

In the Set Variables action, in the Events section, select the event (for example EVENT_FORM_COMPLETE) and set Event serialization to Use event ID, with the value %DL - submissionId%. No code is needed. Keep the ID under 20 characters.

Send the event and the ID through the Analytics data in the event (events: 'EVENT_FORM_COMPLETE:<id>'), or use the datastream's mapping. Check how your datastream passes events. Edge has its own event ID for deduplicating requests; do not confuse the two.

In Processing Rules, set the event with the serial value from context data submissionId.

GA4 has no event serialization. Prevent duplicates instead:

  • Fire the event only from the form_complete push, not on page load of the thank-you page.
  • In the GTM tag, add a trigger exception: do not fire if a first-party cookie or sessionStorage value equals submissionId (a small Custom JavaScript variable can check this).
  • In GA4 reports, count unique submission_id values with an exploration if you need exact numbers.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Submit once: the event has an ID
  • [ ] Refresh the thank-you page: the report counts it once
  • [ ] A second real submission gets a different ID

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Serialization works per event and per report suite. Test it on the event in the report, not only in the debugger, because duplicates are removed during processing.

docs.title: File Downloads
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: Which guides, reports and brochures people download.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text:
Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars 3 EVAR_FILE_NAME, EVAR_FILE_TITLE, EVAR_FILE_URL Props 0 Events 1 EVENT_FILE_DOWNLOAD Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 3 File Name, File Title, File URL Events 1 file_download

The link text goes into the custom link name of the beacon, so it needs no variable.

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: When the visitor clicks a link that downloads a resource (PDF guides, setup guides, profiles, spreadsheets).

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM) Data element (Data Layer Computed State) Path DL - fileTitle, DL - fileName, DL - fileLinkText, DL - fileLinkURL fileTitle, fileName, fileLinkText, fileLinkURL Rule Trigger Actions ACDL - Link: File Download by "file_download" Data layer event file_download Set Variables: EVAR_FILE_NAME, EVAR_FILE_TITLE, EVAR_FILE_URL, event EVENT_FILE_DOWNLOAD. Send Beacon: link type Download Link, link name %DL - fileLinkText%

XDM object: eventType web.webinteraction.linkClicks, web.webInteraction.type download, name = DL - fileTitle, URL = DL - fileLinkURL, linkClicks.value 1. Add a custom field for the file name. Map the three fields to the eVars in the Analytics mapping.

Processing Rules: action name file_download sets EVENT_FILE_DOWNLOAD. Context data fileName, fileTitle, fileLinkURL set EVAR_FILE_NAME, EVAR_FILE_TITLE, EVAR_FILE_URL.

Item Setup Variables DLV - fileTitle, DLV - fileName, DLV - fileLinkText, DLV - fileLinkURL Trigger CE - file_download Tag GA4 - File Download, event file_download, parameters file_title, file_name, link_text, link_url GA4 Admin Register file_title, file_name, link_url as custom dimensions

Turn off enhanced measurement file downloads

GA4 collects file_download automatically (with its own file_name and link_url parameters). Turn off File downloads in enhanced measurement, or each download is counted twice.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Each file type sends one hit
  • [ ] File name has no extension and no query string
  • [ ] Link text and URL match what the visitor clicked
  • [ ] Right-click "Save as" is not counted. Tell clients this is a known gap

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: A download link that also triggers universal_click must send only file_download.

docs.title: Form Tracking
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: How many people start a form, how far they get, how many finish, and where errors happen. Forms are usually the main conversion on a site.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text:
Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars 4 EVAR_FORM_ID, EVAR_FORM_TYPE, EVAR_FORM_NAME, EVAR_FORM_STEP Props 0 Events 4 EVENT_FORM_START, EVENT_FORM_STEP, EVENT_FORM_COMPLETE, EVENT_FORM_ERROR Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 4 Form ID, Form Type, Form Name, Form Step Events 4 form_start, form_step, form_complete, form_error

Single-step forms need only start and complete. Skip the step and error events and their variables if the client does not need them.

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text:
Event Fires when form_start The visitor's first ever interaction with any field in the form. Once per form per visit form_step A step is completed and the next screen is shown (multi-step forms) form_complete After the success response (HTTP 200) is received, meaning the submission was accepted. Not when the button is clicked form_error A validation or submission error is shown to the visitor

Forms with a topic or type selector

If the form name depends on a dropdown (for example "Select a topic") and the visitor changes it, fire form_start again with the new formName.

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM)

Data elements (Adobe Client Data Layer extension, type Data Layer Computed State). Turn on Force lowercase value and Remove extra whitespace.

Name Path DL - formId formId DL - formType formType DL - formName formName DL - formStep formStep DL - submissionId submissionId

Rules. Trigger: Adobe Client Data Layer, Data pushed, event form_start (the label may differ slightly by extension version).

Rule Trigger event Set Variables action Then ACDL - Form: Start by "form_start" form_start EVAR_FORM_ID, EVAR_FORM_TYPE, EVAR_FORM_NAME = the data elements. Event EVENT_FORM_START Send Beacon, custom link, name Form Start ACDL - Form: Step by "form_step" form_step As above plus EVAR_FORM_STEP. Event EVENT_FORM_STEP Send Beacon, Form Step ACDL - Form: Complete by "form_complete" form_complete As start. Event EVENT_FORM_COMPLETE with event serialization set to %DL - submissionId% Send Beacon, Form Complete ACDL - Form: Error by "form_error" form_error As step. Event EVENT_FORM_ERROR Send Beacon, Form Error

No custom code is needed. The serialization option is in the event field of the Set Variables action. It stops a refresh of the thank-you page counting twice (see Event Serialization).

  1. Create an XDM object data element per event, for example XDM - Form Complete, with eventType set to an agreed value (form.complete) and your form fields filled from the DL - data elements.
  2. Rule: same trigger as the AppMeasurement tab. Action: Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK, Send event, with that XDM object.
  3. Map the fields to the Analytics variables, either with Processing Rules on the context data, or by sending data.__adobe.analytics in the event's Data object.
XDM field (in your tenant namespace) Source Analytics variable form.id DL - formId EVAR_FORM_ID form.type DL - formType EVAR_FORM_TYPE form.name DL - formName EVAR_FORM_NAME form.step DL - formStep EVAR_FORM_STEP eventType Event EVENT_FORM_*

Add the custom form field group and the event type values to your schema first.

Developers send the calls in the spec above. In Adobe Analytics, add Processing Rules for the report suite (Admin > Report Suites > Edit Settings > General > Processing Rules):

Condition Set Action name equals form_start EVENT_FORM_START Action name equals form_step EVENT_FORM_STEP Action name equals form_complete EVENT_FORM_COMPLETE, serial from context data submissionId Action name equals form_error EVENT_FORM_ERROR Context data formId exists EVAR_FORM_ID = formId Context data formType exists EVAR_FORM_TYPE = formType Context data formName exists EVAR_FORM_NAME = formName Context data formStep exists EVAR_FORM_STEP = formStep

If the app sends data through the Edge Network instead, follow the Web SDK tab and send the same fields in the XDM event.

Variables (type Data Layer Variable, Data Layer Version 2): DLV - formId, DLV - formType, DLV - formName, DLV - formStep, DLV - submissionId.

Triggers (type Custom Event): CE - form_start, CE - form_step, CE - form_complete, CE - form_error, each with the event name as the trigger name.

Tags (type GA4 Event): one per trigger, event name equal to the trigger's event. Add event parameters:

Parameter Value form_id {{DLV - formId}} form_type {{DLV - formType}} form_name {{DLV - formName}} form_step {{DLV - formStep}} (step and error tags) submission_id {{DLV - submissionId}} (complete tag; used for de-duplication, not as a dimension)

Then, in GA4 Admin > Custom definitions, register form_id, form_type, form_name and form_step as event-scoped custom dimensions, and mark form_complete as a key event.

Turn off enhanced measurement forms

GA4 can collect form_start and form_submit by itself. Turn off Form interactions in enhanced measurement, or you will count starts twice.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Start fires once, not on every field
  • [ ] Changing a form topic fires a new start with the new name
  • [ ] Complete fires only on success, never on a failed submit
  • [ ] Refreshing the thank-you page does not count a second complete
  • [ ] Every push has all its keys
  • [ ] No typed values appear in any request

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Put the form name in the data layer. Do not read the <h1> or page title.
  • One pattern for every form. Do not create a separate set of rules for each form.

docs.title: Marketing Channels
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: Which campaign, ad or email brought a visitor to the site. In Adobe, Marketing Channels reports sort visits into channels (Paid Search, Email, Display and so on) using rules in Admin, and the tracking code in the landing page URL names the exact campaign. In Google Analytics, UTM parameters do the same job.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds Campaign variable 1 Tracking code (s.campaign) eVars 0 (1 optional) EVAR_TRACKING_CODE: only if you need a different expiry or allocation Props 0 Events 0 Other Marketing Channel rules, set once per report suite in Admin Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 0 Uses built-in source, medium and campaign Events 0

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: On the first page of a visit whose URL has the tracking code. Not on reloads or later pages.

docs.title: Values and naming
docs.text:
Adobe tracking code: channel_source_campaign_content, lower case, in the URL parameter cid. Agree one parameter name for all clients.

Good Bad email_newsletter_autumn-promo_hero-button Autumn Promo!! ppc_google_cards-2026_brand cards ppc

Google Analytics: use the standard utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign and utm_content. Do not put customer names or emails in either.

docs.title: Developer specification
docs.text:
Nothing for web developers. The marketing team adds the parameters to campaign links, and the tools read them from the URL. For internal promotions, do not use cid or UTM parameters (see Universal Clickthrough).

For mobile apps, the campaign usually arrives in a deep link. Developers read it and send it:

Mobile apps 
// iOS: when the app opens from a link
func handleDeepLink(_ url: URL) {
    let cid = URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)?
        .queryItems?.first(where: { $0.name == "cid" })?.value
    if let cid = cid {
        MobileCore.track(action: "campaign_open", data: ["trackingCode": cid])
    }
}

// Android
val cid = intent.data?.getQueryParameter("cid")
if (cid != null) MobileCore.trackAction("campaign_open", mapOf("trackingCode" to cid))

docs.title: Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM) Data element Type Setting Query - cid Query String Parameter Parameter cid, convert to lower case Rule Trigger Actions PLR - Global: Page View (add to the existing rule) Page Bottom Set Variables: Campaign = %Query - cid% (and EVAR_TRACKING_CODE if used)

Custom code (only if needed): without it, a page refresh counts the code again. The Common Analytics Plugins extension provides getValOnce:

s.campaign = s.getValOnce(_satellite.getVar('Query - cid'), 's_cid', 0);

Then, in Adobe Analytics, set the Marketing Channel rules (Admin > Report Suites > Edit Settings > Marketing Channels > Marketing Channel Rules). The first rule that matches wins, so order matters.

In the page-view XDM object, set marketing.trackingCode to %Query - cid% (check the field in your schema). Send it only on the first page of the visit. Marketing Channel rules are still set in Admin.

Processing Rule: when action name equals campaign_open, set Campaign = context data trackingCode. Then set the Marketing Channel rules in Admin.

Nothing to build. The Google tag reads the UTM parameters and GA4 builds the Traffic acquisition reports. Check that:

  • The Google tag fires on every page, including the landing page, before any redirect drops the parameters.
  • Campaign links use one agreed UTM format.
  • Internal links never use UTM parameters.

For custom channel groups, create them in GA4 Admin > Data display > Channel groups.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Visit ?cid=test_qa_check_1: the code is sent once
  • [ ] Refresh: it is not sent again
  • [ ] Visit with no cid: nothing is sent
  • [ ] The visit shows in the expected Marketing Channel (after processing)
  • [ ] A redirect on the landing page does not drop the parameters

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Marketing Channels in Adobe need both the tracking code and the rules in Admin. The code alone does not create channels.

docs.title: Page Naming
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: Every page view needs a clear, stable page name. It is the main label in Pathing, Fallout and Page reports. A bad or changing name makes years of data hard to compare.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds Page Name 1 Page name (s.pageName) eVars 1 EVAR_PAGE_NAME: the same name, so it can be used with conversion events Props 0 (1 optional) PROP_PAGE_NAME: only if you need pathing on a prop Events 0 Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 1 Page Name Events 0 Uses the built-in page_view

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: On every page view and every virtual page view (single-page apps and pages that change content without reloading).

docs.title: Values and naming
docs.text:
Format: site:section:subsection:page, lower case, colon between levels, hyphens inside words, under 100 characters.

Good Bad acme:sg:personal:cards:credit-cards Credit Cards acme:sg:business:loans:overview https://acme.com/business/loans/index.html

Never use the full URL, the page title (marketing edits titles), query strings, IDs or personal data.

docs.title: Developer specification
docs.text:
Default: nothing for developers. The tagging team builds the name from the URL path in one data element (see Tagging setup). Use the push below only when the name cannot be worked out from the URL, for example for single-page apps or pages with generic URLs. The same push can also carry the site section keys.

Adobe websites (adobeDataLayer)Google Analytics websites (dataLayer)Mobile apps 
window.adobeDataLayer = window.adobeDataLayer || [];
window.adobeDataLayer.push({
  'event': 'page_view',
  'pageName': '<page name>'
});

window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
window.dataLayer.push({
  'event': 'page_view_custom',
  'pageName': '<page name>'
});

MobileCore.track(state: "acme:sg:app:cards:credit-cards", data: nil)

MobileCore.trackState("acme:sg:app:cards:credit-cards", null)
Key What it holds Example pageName The page name in the format above acme:sg:personal:cards:credit-cards

Run the push once the page content has loaded, and again for each virtual page view.

docs.title: Tagging setup
QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Name matches the format on 5 page types (home, listing, article, form, error)
  • [ ] Only one page view per page
  • [ ] The name does not change after a language switch, unless intended
  • [ ] Virtual page views send a new name

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Changing page names later splits your reports. Agree the format with the client before launch.

docs.title: QA and Debugging
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Tool Use for Adobe Experience Platform Debugger (browser extension) See which Launch library loaded and what each hit contains Browser developer tools, Network tab Filter /b/ss/ for AppMeasurement hits and /ee/ for Web SDK hits _satellite.setDebug(true) in the console See which Launch rules fire and why adobeDataLayer and adobeDataLayer.getState() in the console See the pushes and the combined values Assurance Mobile SDK sessions Tool Use for GTM Preview mode (Tag Assistant) See the data layer events, variables and which tags fired GA4 DebugView (Admin > DebugView) See events and parameters arrive in near real time dataLayer in the console See the pushes

docs.title: Before testing
docs.text:
• Use the staging library and a test report suite or property. Do not test on production data.
  • Use a private window, or clear cookies.

docs.title: Standard test for every feature
docs.text:
1. The developer's push appears in the data layer, with every key.
  2. The right rule or tag fires, once.
  3. The hit contains the correct values and the correct events.
  4. Refresh and repeat the action. Check nothing is counted twice.
  5. No personal data appears in any request.

docs.title: Site Search
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: What visitors look for, how many get results, and where search fails. Useful for content gaps, navigation fixes and measuring search-driven conversions.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars 3 EVAR_SEARCH_TERM, EVAR_SEARCH_RESULTS (number of results as a range), EVAR_SEARCH_TYPE (where the search started) Props 1 PROP_SEARCH_TERM, for pathing Events 2 EVENT_SEARCH (every search), EVENT_SEARCH_NULL (zero results) Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 2 Search Results, Search Type. The term uses GA4's built-in search_term Events 2 view_search_results, search_no_results

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: Once, when the results are shown. Not when the visitor types or presses the button, because the result count is not known yet. If zero results are shown, push the no-results event as well.

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] A search with results sends one search hit and no null event
  • [ ] A search with no results also sends the null event
  • [ ] The term is lower case and trimmed
  • [ ] Typing an email address into search does not reach any tool
  • [ ] Refreshing the results page does not count a second search

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Use searchType suggestion for type-ahead suggestions so you can compare them with full searches.

docs.title: Site Sections
docs.text: Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: Groups pages into areas such as Personal, Business and Support, so the client can see traffic and conversions by area without reading a list of pages.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds Channel variable 1 Level 1 section (s.channel) eVars 1 EVAR_SITE_SECTION: level 1, so conversions can be split by section Props 3 PROP_SECTION_L2, PROP_SECTION_L3, PROP_SECTION_L4: sub-sections, for traffic and pathing Events 0 Other Hierarchy variable (hier1) is optional Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 3 Section L2, L3, L4. Level 1 uses GA4's built-in content_group Events 0

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: On every page view, together with the page name.

docs.title: Values and naming
docs.text:
Use the same words as the page name, in the same order.

Page name Level 1 L2 L3 L4 acme:sg:personal:cards:credit-cards personal cards credit-cards acme:sg:business:loans:overview business loans overview

Leave unused levels empty. Do not write n/a or none.

docs.title: Developer specification
docs.text:
Default: nothing for developers. The tagging team splits the page name (see Page Naming) into the levels. Use the keys below only if the sections cannot be worked out from the name.

Adobe websites (adobeDataLayer)Google Analytics websites (dataLayer)Mobile apps 
window.adobeDataLayer = window.adobeDataLayer || [];
window.adobeDataLayer.push({
  'event': 'page_view',
  'pageName': '<page name>',
  'siteSection1': '<section>',
  'siteSection2': '<sub section>',
  'siteSection3': '<sub sub section>',
  'siteSection4': '<level 4>'
});

window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
window.dataLayer.push({
  'event': 'page_view_custom',
  'pageName': '<page name>',
  'siteSection1': '<section>',
  'siteSection2': '<sub section>',
  'siteSection3': '<sub sub section>',
  'siteSection4': '<level 4>'
});

MobileCore.track(state: "acme:sg:app:cards:credit-cards", data: [
    "siteSection1": "app", "siteSection2": "cards", "siteSection3": "credit-cards"
])
Key What it holds Example siteSection1 to siteSection4 Levels 1 to 4. Empty text for unused levels personal, cards, credit-cards, ``

docs.title: Tagging setup
QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Levels match the page name on every template
  • [ ] Empty levels send nothing
  • [ ] A new area of the site does not fall into a blank section

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Props do not persist between hits, so they are for traffic and pathing. Use the eVar when you want to link a section to a later conversion.

docs.title: Video Tracking
docs.text:
Status: Draft · Owner: Parikshit Shinge · Last reviewed: 29-Oct-2026

Not tested yet

This tag started as a proposal and has not been tested on a live property. Check the open questions under Notes before you use it on a project.

docs.title: What this tracks and why
docs.text: How many people start, finish and drop out of videos on the site.

docs.title: Variables required
docs.text: Adobe AnalyticsGoogle Analytics 4 Type How many What each one holds eVars 2 EVAR_VIDEO_NAME, EVAR_VIDEO_MILESTONE Props 0 Events 5 EVENT_VIDEO_START, EVENT_VIDEO_25, EVENT_VIDEO_50, EVENT_VIDEO_75, EVENT_VIDEO_COMPLETE Type How many What each one holds Custom dimensions 2 Video Name, Video Milestone Events 1 video_milestone. Not video_progress: GA4's built-in YouTube tracking already uses video_start, video_progress and video_complete

docs.title: When to fire
docs.text: Start when the video plays for the first time. Then once at 25%, 50%, 75% and complete. Not again if the visitor replays or seeks back.

docs.title: Developer specification
Tagging setup
docs.text:
Adobe Analytics (AppMeasurement)Adobe Web SDK (XDM)Adobe Mobile SDKGoogle Analytics 4 (GTM)

One rule ACDL - Video: Milestone by "video_milestone", with five conditions or five rules (one per milestone), each setting its event and the two eVars.

Adobe has standard media events in XDM (for example media.play). Check Adobe's Media Analytics guidance before adding custom events.

Consider the Media extension before building custom processing rules.

Trigger on video_milestone; GA4 Event tag with parameters video_name, video_milestone. Turn off enhanced measurement Video engagement if you track it yourself.

docs.title: QA checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Each milestone fires once
  • [ ] Seeking forward does not skip or duplicate milestones

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• 29-Oct-2026: moved from Proposals to Core tags as a Draft tag. Counts added to the totals.
  • 29-Oct-2026: GA4 event name set to video_milestone (was video_progress in the Variables table), to match the data layer push and avoid GA4's built-in video events.
  • Open question: use Adobe Media Analytics instead of custom events?
  • Open question: which video players does each client use?
